[USER] User inquired about the number of moons of Uranus and their names.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Uranus has 27 known moons. Their names are Miranda, Ariel, Umbriel, Titania, Oberon, Francisco, Caliban, Stephano, Trinculo, Sycorax, Prospero, Setebos, Ferdinand, Mab, Cupid, Perdita, Portia, Rosalind, Juliet, Belinda, Puck, Cressida, Desdemona, Bianca, Ophelia, Cordelia, and Margaret.  
[USER] User expressed surprise at the number of moons Uranus has.  
[USER] User asked if any of Uranus' moons have interesting features.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Some of Uranus' moons have interesting features:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Miranda has large, steep cliffs and canyons indicating significant tectonic activity in the past.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Ariel has deep grooves indicating the presence of a subsurface ocean.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Umbriel has a dark, heavily cratered surface.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Titania and Oberon have large impact basins and distinctive geological features such as canyons, fault scarps, and mountains.  
[USER] User found the information about the moons' features to be really cool.  
[USER] User inquired if any of Uranus' moons have potential for future exploration by spacecraft.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] There are no planned missions to Uranus at the moment, but some moons could be potential exploration targets:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Miranda is suggested as a particularly interesting target due to its unique surface features.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Ariel, believed to have a subsurface ocean, and Titania, with various geological features, could also be attractive exploration targets.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Exploring Uranus and its moons would be challenging due to the considerable distance from Earth and the extreme cold and radiation environment.
